# Jubilees Chapter 47 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Moses born; hidden; found by Pharaoh's daughter; his early life

---

**47:1** In the seventh week, in the seventh year, in the first year, in the forty-seventh jubilee, the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, and the angel of the presence spoke to Moses according to the word of the LORD.

**47:2** And there arose a new king over Egypt who oppressed the children of Israel. And he said: "Let us kill their males, lest they multiply, and lest they cause war against us."

**47:3** And Pharaoh commanded that every male child born of the sons of Israel should be cast into the river, to drown them.

**47:4** And a man of the tribe of Levi went and took to wife a daughter of Levi, and she conceived and bore a son. And she saw that he was good, and she hid him three months.

**47:5** And she was not able to hide him any longer. She took for him an ark of bulrushes and plastered it within and without with pitch, and put the child therein and laid him in the flags by the river's brink.

**47:6** And his sister stood afar off to learn what would be done to him.

**47:7** And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself in the river, and her maidens went along by the river's side. And she saw the ark among the flags and sent her maid to fetch it.

**47:8** And she opened it and saw the child, and behold the child wept. And she had compassion on him and said: "This is one of the Hebrew children."

**47:9** And his sister came near and said to the daughter of Pharaoh: "Shall I go and call thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee?" And Pharaoh's daughter said: "Go." And the maid went and called the child's mother.

**47:10** And Pharaoh's daughter said to her: "Take this child and nurse it for me, and I will give thee thy wages." And the woman took the child and nursed it.

**47:11** And when the child had grown up, she brought him to the daughter of Pharaoh and he became her son. And she called his name Moses, saying: "For I drew him out of the water."

**47:12** And in those days Moses grew up in Pharaoh's house, and he was loved by Pharaoh greatly. And he was taught all the wisdom of the Egyptians.

**47:13** And Mastema came and wanted to kill Moses. And the LORD said to him: "I have not yet fulfilled his time." And Mastema departed from before him.

---

*EMET notes: The Moses birth narrative follows Exodus 2:1-10 very closely in the Ge'ez, with the important addition of Mastema's attempt to kill the infant Moses (v.13) — a motif that recurs in ch.48. The name etymology "I drew him out of the water" follows the Hebrew moshe/mashah etymology. The framing of the whole book (v.1) places the narration as spoken from Sinai.*
